title: Carbon monoxide in WASP-39 b
subtitle: A computational reproduction of the JWST/NIRSpec G395H sub-band experiment
question: Do the model-selected CO absorption bands show a larger transit depth than adjacent comparison bands in the released spectrum?
dataMode: Grant et al. (2023) released derived products

figures.label: Released native-resolution spectrum and archived model curves
Exact in-band and out-of-band samples used in the test
Primary contrast with Welch and bootstrap uncertainty
Descriptive residual diagnostic for the fixed curves

methods: Load the deposited spectrum and the authors’ exact CO sub-band arrays; verify each file against its manifest SHA-256.
Estimate the in-band minus out-of-band mean transit-depth contrast and reproduce the one-sided unequal-variance Welch test.
Quantify uncertainty with a deterministic 10,000-resample within-group bootstrap and an exploratory label-permutation check.
Probe spectral leverage using two broad wavelength zones and deletion of each contiguous selected wavelength run.
Compare the two archived curves with χ² only as a descriptive diagnostic; no model is refit and no AIC/BIC is claimed.
limitations: The selected bands are informed by atmospheric models; this is not a blind molecule search.
The reproduction starts from released derived spectra rather than detector ramps or uncalibrated exposures.
Neighbouring native-resolution pixels can be correlated, so the nominal Welch probability is conditional on the test assumptions.
The archive contains 145 out-of-band values, whereas the article text reports 148; the released arrays are used unchanged.
Fixed-curve χ² differences do not identify a Bayes factor, an abundance posterior, or a detection significance.
